findings.text: Guest virtual system write helper is exposed for nested emulation use. It requests a host L1 data flush before delegating to a page oriented helper with write permission and a caller supplied fault record, returning continuation, fault propagation, or IO needed indications.

VMXON emulation entry validates host state and operand before entering VMX operation. It raises undefined opcode when virtualization enable is clear, injects protection fault for nonzero privilege or invalid control state, reports invalid failure for bad address or revision mismatch, otherwise records the activation pointer and enters operation with success indication.

VMXOFF, VMCLEAR, VMPTRLD and VMPTRST handlers form the VMX lifecycle interface. VMXOFF releases nested state and requests event processing when pending initialization signals exist. VMCLEAR and VMPTRLD validate operand address and reject the activation pointer, while VMPTRST stores the current pointer to caller memory. All first enforce a permission check.

VMREAD and VMWRITE handlers emulate guest access to virtual machine control fields. They enforce permission, verify a loaded control structure and link validity, resolve field encoding to an offset, transfer a zero extended value between register or guest memory and the control image, and report unsupported component or read only violations through failure indications.
VMLAUNCH and VMRESUME handlers are thin entries that delegate to a shared nested run routine with a flag distinguishing initial launch from resume.

INVEPT and INVVPID handlers emulate translation and process identifier invalidations. They raise undefined opcode when host advertises no support, enforce permission, decode invalidation type from a register selector, fetch a fixed size memory operand unconditionally, validate type and operand, perform root or processor specific flushing, then signal success.

VMXON enforces a strict priority: virtualization enable and privilege checks precede already active failure, which precedes host control validity and feature control checks, which precede operand fetch and address plus revision validation. Real mode and compatibility checks are left to hardware except for the explicitly emulated enable bit.

Control structure pointers must denote a valid paged address distinct from the activation pointer. VMPTRLD additionally requires successful guest cache setup, correct revision identifier, and shadow support when requested, and reloads the cached image only when the pointer differs from the current one. VMCLEAR clears launch state to zero for the targeted image.

VMREAD, VMWRITE, VMPTRST, INVEPT and INVVPID share an instruction information decoding convention. Field or type selectors come from register indices extracted from high bits of the information word, register versus memory form is indicated by a single flag bit, memory length follows guest sixty four bit mode, and memory effective address is resolved through a common helper before guest access.

Shadow field membership is determined by generated lists for readable writable and read only sets. Non guest writes to non shadowed fields first synchronize rare state into the cached image, mask access rights bytes to architecturally preserved bits, update the image, mirror read only shadowed fields into hardware shadow state when enabled, and mark the image dirty. Read only enforcement is relaxed when the guest advertises write any support.

INVEPT type support derives from capability bits shifted to a mask and INVVPID support from a masked and shifted capability field; out of range or unsupported types fail as invalid operand. INVEPT context form validates the supplied pointer and frees only matching current and previous roots while global form frees all. INVVPID requires sixteen bit zero extended identifier, nonzero identifier except for all context form, and canonical address for individual address form.

Guest virtual writes proceed page by page. Each iteration translates the current virtual address through the vCPU walk callback, propagates a fault when translation yields an invalid physical address, writes the page bounded chunk to guest physical memory, and converts host write errors into an IO needed result while advancing pointers until all bytes complete.

Enlightened control pointer presence changes behavior: normal VMPTRLD and VMPTRST take an early exit path when it is valid, VMCLEAR delegates to an enlightened handler that can suppress normal processing, and VMREAD switches to an enlightened field table and image instead of the regular control image.

Updates to the hardware shadow control image during VMWRITE are performed with preemption disabled across a sequence that loads the shadow image, performs the field write, clears it, and reloads the previously loaded image before reenabling preemption.

INVVPID processor specific flushing pins the calling processor across tracking checks and synchronization. If the stored nested control was last loaded on another processor, tracking is invalidated to defer the flush; otherwise address specific or full context synchronization for the effective nested identifier occurs before unpinning.

INVEPT operand holds two eight byte values for pointer and address and INVVPID operand holds two eight byte values for identifier and linear address. VMPTRLD inspects a header containing revision identifier and shadow indicator. Nested state tracks activation pointer, current pointer with invalid sentinel, cached control image, shadow synchronization need, dirty flag, posted interrupt vector with negative cleared value, and MSR bitmap recalculation request.

VMX operation moves from inactive to active on successful VMXON which stores activation pointer and enters operation, and returns to inactive on VMXOFF which frees nested state. Current pointer moves from invalid to loaded on VMPTRLD which enables shadow controls and marks dirty state, persists across VMREAD and VMWRITE, and returns to invalid on VMCLEAR of the current image or explicit release which flushes the cached image to guest memory and frees all guest translation roots.

Nested extended page table state supports selective and global invalidation plus list based switching. Context invalidation frees only roots matching the supplied pointer while global frees all. Switching reads an eight byte entry indexed by low guest register from a guest page list, ignores requests targeting the active pointer, otherwise validates and installs the new pointer, notifies paging logic, and requests guest translation flush when process identifiers are unavailable.

VMCLEAR deliberately ignores guest write errors when clearing launch state, treating absent backing as architecturally permitted. VMPTRLD treats reads from unbacked pages as all ones and therefore as revision mismatch rather than memory failure. VMREAD permits enlightened control reads as a compatibility workaround despite specification stating unsupported, warning if invoked in guest mode. Access rights bytes are masked on write to hide host dependent reserved bit behavior.

Control revision identifier, invalid physical address sentinel, page shift and size, control image size, launch state offset, VMX error numbers for VMXON, VMCLEAR, VMPTRLD, unsupported component, read only violation and invalid invalidation operand, feature control lock and enable bits, secondary execution shadow, EPT and VPID bits, miscellaneous write any bit, EPT and VPID capability and extent values, exception vectors, and translation root selectors are ABI facts referenced by these paths.
